questions.stem: Which of the following is a unit for a vector quantity?
A lamp has a constant power input and a constant efficiency. Which row of the table describes how the useful power output and total energy output vary with time?
Which of the following is always true of the forces in a Newton's third law pair?

options.text: The forces act on the same object.
The forces act in the same direction.
The forces have the same magnitude.

questions.stem: A ball bearing falls through oil at a terminal velocity. Which row of the table is correct when the temperature of the oil decreases?

A balloon moves upwards at terminal velocity. The forces acting on the balloon are upthrust U, viscous drag D and weight W. Which of the following statements about the magnitudes of the forces acting on the balloon is correct?

A plank of wood has weight W. The plank rests on two supports. The forces from the supports on the plank are $ F_{\mathrm{A}} $ and $ F_{\mathrm{B}} $ , as shown. Which of the following vector equations gives the relationship between $ F_{\mathrm{A}} $ , $ F_{\mathrm{B}} $ and W?

A student uses a piece of string to attach a mass of 0.4kg to a mass of 0.5kg. She then places the string over a pulley, as shown. Which of the following gives the acceleration of the 0.5kg mass in $ \mathrm{m s}^{-2} $?
The table shows information about two wires made from different metals. Which of the following is the extension of Q?
The acceleration-time graph for the motion of an object is shown. Which of the following could be the displacement-time graph for the motion of the object?

Two objects, R and S, are falling vertically and accelerating due to gravity. Air resistance is negligible. R has mass m and S has mass 2m. Initially, each object has momentum p. After time t object R has momentum 2p. Which of the following gives the momentum of object S after time t?
A lorry has a mass of 4500kg. The forward force on the lorry is 6700N. The total resistive force on the lorry is 900 N. Calculate the acceleration of the lorry.

A sailing boat is moving through water. The force of the wind on the boat is 350N towards north. The force of the water on the boat is 410N at an angle of $ 1 2 0^{\circ} $ from north, as shown. Determine the magnitude and direction of the resultant force on the boat using a scaled vector diagram.
answerPrompts: Angle of resultant force from north

questions.stem: A student used two different methods to investigate the acceleration of a freely falling object.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the first method, the student dropped a ball from rest at a known height. He used a stopwatch to measure the time taken for the ball to reach the ground. He repeated this several times. He then calculated the mean acceleration of the ball. Explain why there was a large uncertainty in the calculated value of acceleration.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In the second method, the student positioned light gates near the top and bottom of a transparent vertical tube. He dropped a metal cylinder into the tube, as shown. The time taken for the metal cylinder to pass through each light gate was recorded by a data logger. The student measured the distance between the light gates.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Give one other measurement needed to determine the acceleration of the metal cylinder.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: The speed of the metal cylinder through the first light gate was $ 1.39\mathrm{m s}^{-1}. $ The speed of the metal cylinder through the second light gate was $ 2.96\mathrm{m s}^{-1}. $ The distance between the light gates was 355mm. Calculate the acceleration of the metal cylinder. Acceleration

questions.stem: Two rocks in outer space are moving at different speeds along the same path.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the principle of conservation of momentum.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Rock A has a mass of 43 kg and a velocity of $ 7. 8 \mathrm{~ m s}^{-1}. $ Rock B has a mass of 56kg and moves in the same direction as rock A. The kinetic energy of rock B is $ 4. 1 \times1 0^{3} \mathrm{J}. $ Rock B collides with rock A. After the collision, rock B continues to move in the same direction with a momentum of $ 5 3 0 \mathrm{k g} \mathrm{m s}^{-1}. $ Calculate the new velocity of rock A.

questions.stem: A student investigated a spring. The student measured the unstretched length of the spring. The student suspended different objects from the spring, as shown. She measured the new length of the spring each time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The unstretched length of the spring was 0.250 m. When the ball was suspended from the spring, the length of the spring was 0.295 m. When the 200 g mass was suspended from the spring, the length of the spring was 0.375 m. Calculate the weight of the ball.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The sketch graph shows how the extension $ \Delta x $ of the spring varies with the total force F on the spring. Explain why the elastic strain energy stored by the spring is proportional to $ F^{2}. $

questions.stem: The photograph shows an athlete using a running blade. running blade

parts.label: a
parts.text: The value of the Young modulus for the material used to make the running blade is 19 GPa.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: State which property of the material relates to the Young modulus.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: A sample of the material has a length of 0.450m. In a laboratory test, a compressive stress of 150MPa is applied to the sample. The sample deforms elastically. Determine the new length of the sample.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The running blade is made from a single material. The table shows the compressive breaking stress of three materials used to make different running blades. The cross-sectional area of the running blade is $ 8. 5 \mathrm{c m}^{2} $ . The maximum compressive force that can be applied to the running blade before it breaks is 330kN. Deduce which material the running blade is made from.

questions.stem: A 'lifting bag' is a bag that can be filled with air and used to lift heavy objects from the bottom of the sea. Lifting bags are attached to an object and then filled with air.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A person attaches two spherical lifting bags to a box at the bottom of the sea, as shown. The total weight of the box and two lifting bags filled with air is 2500N. The diameter of each spherical lifting bag is 50cm. Deduce whether the box will lift from the bottom of the sea. density of seawater = 1020kgm $ ^{-3} $

parts.label: b
parts.text: As the person filled the lifting bags, a small bubble of air escaped and moved upwards through the seawater.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Calculate the terminal velocity of the bubble of air predicted by Stokes' law. weight of air in bubble $ = 1. 8 2 \times1 0^{-6} \mathrm{N} $ upthrust on bubble $ = 4. 7 7 \times1 0^{-4} \mathrm{N} $ viscosity of seawater $ = 8. 6 0 \times1 0^{-4} \mathrm{P a s} $ radius of bubble $ = 2. 2 5 \times1 0^{-3} \mathrm{m} $

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Give two reasons why the terminal velocity of the bubble may be different from the value predicted by Stokes' law.

questions.stem: In the sport of bicycle motocross (BMX) a person rides a bicycle over small hills and ramps. The diagram shows three stages, A, B and C, of the motion of the bicycle. In stage A the bicycle moves with constant acceleration on a horizontal surface until time $ T_{\mathrm{A}}. $ In stage B the bicycle moves with constant velocity up a curved ramp until time $ T_{\mathrm{B}} $ In stage C the bicycle leaves the ground. A person rides a bicycle to the top of a hill with enough speed for the bicycle to leave the ground.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the sketch graph for stages A and B. $ ^{*} ( b ) $ Explain how the useful power output of the person varies through stages A, B and C. You should consider energy changes during each stage. Assume that air resistance is negligible.

questions.stem: In the sport of shot put, a person launches a heavy ball called a 'shot' into the air. The photograph shows a person about to launch a shot.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The shot is very dense and has a large mass. Explain why the equations of motion can be used to give an accurate prediction for the path of the shot.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The shot was released from a height of 1.85m above the ground. The shot travelled a horizontal distance of 14.2m before landing on the ground, as shown. The shot moved through the air for a time of 1.61 s.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Show that the horizontal speed of the shot was about $ 8. 8 \mathrm{~ m s}^{-1}. $

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Determine the velocity of the shot at the point it was released.

questions.stem: The photograph shows Tower Bridge, a bridge in London. The middle part of the bridge can be raised in two sections to allow boats to travel along the river. Each section can rotate about a pivot.

parts.label: b

parts.label: b-ii
